meta_title: Integral of 1/(e^x+e^-x) 0 to 1 - NCERT Exemplar Q29
meta_desc: Solve the NCERT Exemplar Class 12 integral of dx/(e^x+e^-x) from 0 to 1 with the substitution e^x=t to reach arctan, plus a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Substitution to Arctan Integrals Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on turning a definite integral into an arctan form by substitution, exactly the method used for this NCERT Exemplar problem. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Definite integration by substitution to an arctan form (Class 12)

questions.q: If you set e<sup>x</sup> = t, what is dt equal to?
questions.explanation: Differentiating t = e<sup>x</sup> gives dt/dx = e<sup>x</sup>, so dt = e<sup>x</sup> dx. That is why we multiply the integrand by e<sup>x</sup>/e<sup>x</sup>.

questions.q: Multiplying numerator and denominator by e<sup>x</sup>, the integrand dx/(e<sup>x</sup>+e<sup>-x</sup>) becomes:
questions.explanation: e<sup>x</sup>(e<sup>x</sup>+e<sup>-x</sup>) = e<sup>2x</sup>+1, so the integrand is e<sup>x</sup> dx/(e<sup>2x</sup>+1) = dt/(1+t<sup>2</sup>) after substitution.

questions.q: As x runs from 0 to 1, the new variable t = e<sup>x</sup> runs from:
questions.explanation: When x = 0, t = e<sup>0</sup> = 1; when x = 1, t = e<sup>1</sup> = e. So the limits change to t: 1 to e.
This is the standard result: the integral of 1/(1+t<sup>2</sup>) is tan<sup>-1</sup> t + C.

questions.q: Putting the pieces together, the value of the integral is:
questions.explanation: Evaluating arctan t from 1 to e gives arctan e - arctan 1 = arctan e - π/4.
tan(π/4) = 1, so arctan 1 = π/4. This supplies the lower-limit term.

questions.q: The general formula for the integral of 1/(a<sup>2</sup>+x<sup>2</sup>) is:
questions.explanation: The integral of 1/(a<sup>2</sup>+x<sup>2</sup>) is (1/a) tan<sup>-1</sup>(x/a) + C. Here a = 1, which reduces it to arctan t.

questions.q: The denominator e<sup>x</sup>+e<sup>-x</sup> can also be written as:
questions.explanation: By definition cosh x = (e<sup>x</sup>+e<sup>-x</sup>)/2, so e<sup>x</sup>+e<sup>-x</sup> = 2 cosh x. Recognising this is another route to the same integral.

faq.q: Which substitution solves the integral of dx/(e^x+e^-x)?
faq.a: Set e<sup>x</sup> = t, so dt = e<sup>x</sup> dx. After multiplying the integrand by e<sup>x</sup>/e<sup>x</sup>, it collapses to dt/(1+t<sup>2</sup>), whose antiderivative is arctan t.

faq.q: What is the final value of the definite integral from 0 to 1?
faq.a: The limits become t = 1 to t = e, so the integral equals arctan e - arctan 1, which is arctan e - π/4.

faq.q: Why do the limits change from 0 and 1 to 1 and e?
faq.a: The substitution replaces x with t = e<sup>x</sup>. When x = 0, t = 1; when x = 1, t = e. In a definite integral you convert the limits so no back-substitution is needed.

faq.q: Is there a way to solve it without substitution?
faq.a: You can recognise e<sup>x</sup>+e<sup>-x</sup> = 2 cosh x and use hyperbolic identities, but the e<sup>x</sup> = t substitution is faster and is the method NCERT Exemplar expects for Class 12.
